disposition_reason: Tables 2 and 3 print mean lead, chromium and copper for two locally produced alcoholic herbal bitters bought in three Ashanti Region towns, with an unresolved unit problem.

study.design: Consumer survey (n=300) then market sampling of the two most consumed locally produced alcoholic herbal bitters
study.market: Ashanti-Mampong, Nsuta and Agona, Ashanti Region, Ghana
study.method: Aqua regia digestion of 1 mL to dryness at 180 °C, reconstitution to 50 mL; Zeeman AAS (Varian SpectrAA 220Z) for Pb, Cr, Cu
study.qa: Certipur mixed standard IV (CRM 111355) processed through digestion: recoveries Pb 98.20%, Cr 97.67%, Cu 99.80%; blanks

unresolved: All drink results are printed in mg/mL, giving lead of 0.28-6.56 mg/mL (280-6560 mg/L), which is implausible; the intended unit (possibly mg/L or µg/mL) cannot be determined, so values carry an integrity flag and no unit conversion was made.
Abstract and text describe recoveries 97.67% (Cr) to 99.80% (Pb) while Table 1 gives Pb 98.20% and Cu 99.80%.
130 samples (65 per drink) were bought but the number per town is not stated.
LOD not stated; collection dates not stated.
Manifest note says 'Pb 0.28 to 0.45 mg/mL in one bitters'; the second bitters (CGL) has Pb 5.6-6.5 mg/mL, and Cr and Cu are also reported.
